symbols.name: axis index
symbols.meaning: The index of one transform axis, an integer from 1 to D.
symbols.quote: Let $\sigma$ be the index of an axis, with $1\le\sigma\le D$, and let $t_\sigma$ be the length of axis $\sigma$.

symbols.name: output array
symbols.meaning: The array of values that the multidimensional transform produces from X.
symbols.quote: Let $X$ be the input array and $Y$ the output array.

symbols.name: input position
symbols.meaning: A tuple of D coordinates labelling one position in the input array X.
symbols.quote: A position in $X$ is $\varrho=(\varrho_1,\dots,\varrho_D)$ with $0\le\varrho_\sigma<t_\sigma$ for every $\sigma$, and a position in $Y$ is $\varpi=(\varpi_1,\dots,\varpi_D)$ with the same bounds.

symbols.name: output position
symbols.meaning: A tuple of D coordinates labelling one position in the output array Y.
symbols.quote: A position in $X$ is $\varrho=(\varrho_1,\dots,\varrho_D)$ with $0\le\varrho_\sigma<t_\sigma$ for every $\sigma$, and a position in $Y$ is $\varpi=(\varpi_1,\dots,\varpi_D)$ with the same bounds.

symbols.name: multidimensional transform
symbols.meaning: The map sending the input array X to the output array Y by the multidimensional transform formula.
symbols.quote: Let $\mathcal F$ denote the multidimensional transform, which sends $X$ to $Y=\mathcal F X$ by the formula below.

symbols.name: radix-two exponent
symbols.meaning: The exponent with t_sigma equal to 2^k, which counts the radix-two levels of the axis transform.
symbols.quote: Let $k$ be the exponent with $t_\sigma=2^k$, so $k$ counts the radix-two levels of the axis (here $k$ means this exponent, not the padded length of earlier pages).

relations.quote: The transform $\mathcal F$ is built from the [discrete Fourier transforms](discrete-fourier-transform.md) $F_{t_1},\dots,F_{t_D}$ by [tensor product](tensor-product.md).
A multidimensional transform is a Fourier transform taken over several [transform axes](transform-axis.md) at once, computed by transforming along one axis at a time.

The one-dimensional transform along axis $\sigma$ is computed by the [radix-two factorization](radix-two-factorization.md) as $k$ levels of butterflies, with multiplications by roots of unity between the levels.
The multidimensional transform is written in the representation of [synthetic polynomial transforms](synthetic-transforms.md).
In this representation, the transform turns roots of unity into [signed cyclic shifts](cyclic-shift.md).
